newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice Dept. allows Microsoft to buy WebTV.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice Dept. allows Microsoft to buy WebTV.

text.p: The Justice Department said Friday it has approved the proposed acquisition by computer software giant Microsoft Corp. of WebTV Networks Inc. in a deal valued at $425 million.

After what it described as a "thorough investigation," the Justice Department said it had closed the probe into whether the acquisition would violate antitrust laws and decided not to challenge the deal, which was announced in April.

"The investigation confirmed that a number of other companies, several of whom are significant participants in the computer or consumer electronics industries, have or will soon enter the market with competitive products and alternative technologies," the department said in a brief statement.
The Justice Department in May had requested additional information about the deal after a number of Microsoft's competitors complained it could lessen competition.

WebTV designs the specifications for TV set-top boxes and built-in television connections that allow for accessing the Internet. It offers Internet service through agreements with service providers that supply connections around the nation.
Steve Perlman, WebTV's chief executive officer, said this week that he expects to reach 250,000 subscribers by the end of the year, more than double the current number of users. MSFT.O
